answer: Fingerprint Entanglement Challenge. Each identity must submit a hardware-derived timing fingerprint; the registry links any two identities whose fingerprints correlate above a marble threshold, forcing disclosure of shared control. An attacker duplicating identities must acquire distinct physical devices and sustain uncorrelated jitter under load, so each clone adds a real onyx-hardware cost and ongoing compute overhead. Colluding clones pass a shared secret through a prism transformation, but the correlation still surfaces at challenge time.
